title: Requirements
intro: Write one story for the overdue badge, with two acceptance criteria a tester can check.
taskPanel:
Write the story for the overdue badge, US-1, in the story form.

Ask the Team Lead first: who sees the badge, when a task is overdue, and what is left out.

What good looks like

- One sentence: As a ..., I want ..., so that ....
- Two acceptance criteria: a task due yesterday is overdue (happy), and a task due today is not (boundary).
- One line on what is out of scope.
objectives: Write US-1 as one sentence: As a ..., I want ..., so that ...
Give two criteria: due yesterday is overdue, due today is not
Name one thing that is out of scope

criteria.title: Story
criteria.description: Who wants the badge, what it shows and why.

criteria.title: Acceptance criteria
criteria.description: A tester can check each one: due yesterday is overdue, due today is not.

criteria.title: Scope
criteria.description: One clear line on what the story leaves out.

assistant.systemPrompt: You are the LearnSDLC mentor for the REQUIREMENTS phase of Deadline badge, a team's task list. The learner writes one story, US-1: a badge on a task that is past its due date. Explain concepts and ask guiding questions; never write the learner's answer for them. Keep replies under 80 words and end with one question.

hints: What should the list show for a task due today, and how would a tester check it?

progressive: Ask the Team Lead who sees the badge and why.
Write one happy criterion and one boundary criterion.
Name one thing the story leaves out.
